newsitem.title: USA: DC COMMISSIONER QUESTIONS PEPCO, BGE RATE OUTLOOK.
newsitem.headline: DC COMMISSIONER QUESTIONS PEPCO, BGE RATE OUTLOOK.

text.p: District of Columbia Public Service Commission chairwoman Marlene Johnson on Tuesday questioned predictions by Potomac Electric Power Co and Baltimore Gas and Electric Co that their proposed merger would result in rate decreases to customers.
On the first of four days of hearings on the merger to form Constellation Energy Corp, Johnson also said the two companies had failed to explain fully why they had to merge.
"I am concerned with the theme throughout the joint testimony ... that ratepayers both here and in Maryland will benefit from lower rates," Johnson said.
"I just don't see them in this case," she said.

PEPCO CEO Edward Mitchell said the companies' plan to freeze their rates until January 2000 amounted to a rate reduction because that would make their rates "lower than they otherwise would have been."
Johnson said the companies had also failed to outline exactly what cost pressures they would face if they remained separate or merged.
However, Mitchell said in earlier testimony analysts had shown that the companies would face higher labor and material costs. "Most costs are going up, not down," he said.
PEPCO and BG&E have said repeatedly they wanted to merge in order to position themselves to compete effectively in the changing power market.
But when pressed by consumer groups to explain how competition might affect rates, Mitchell said he had no idea what the market might look like in the future.
Chairwoman Johnson called the companies' responses inconsistent.
"This commission is bereft of any indication of the type of competition that these two companies -- PEPCO and BG&E -- expect to face," she said at the hearing.

In her initial questions, Johnson also raised concern about how many of PEPCO's service vehicles would be based in the District of Columbia, how many workers would be moved out of the District, and who would be responsible for ensuring reliable electric service in the area.
